steps: Check the flue gas agitator
It ships pre-installed: remove the cardboard piece and verify the rear pin is in place. Never operate with the agitator removed.

The Flue Gas Agitator comes pre-installed inside the unit. Remove the cardboard piece and verify the rear pin is in place. Do not operate with the agitator removed.

To replace it (part 80003003)

  1. Remove the rear baffle assembly (Baffle Removal, p. 13).
  2. Lift the back of the agitator to free its pin from the hole in the flue opening, and pull it toward the front of the stove.
  3. Lower it down and back to disengage it from the front mounting slots in the flame shield.
  4. Reverse steps 1–3 to install the new agitator.
Fireplace size & hearth
Check the opening against the minimum fireplace dimensions (Figure 12). The non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the opening.

The fireplace's non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the existing fireplace opening.

The minimum fireplace opening dimensions are given only on the Figure 12 drawing on this page; check the opening against it before you start.
Ember protection
Protect combustible flooring with non-combustible material: USA 16" to the firing side (from the glass) and 8" each side of the door opening; Canada 18" and 8" each side of the unit.

Combustible flooring in front of the insert must be protected from hot embers by non-combustible material:

USA16" to the firing side (from the glass) · 8" to each side of the door opening
Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass) · 8" to each side of the unit

Codes: N.F.P.A. 211 (USA), CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada). Figure 13 shows the layout as a drawing.

Optional leveling legs

Leveling bolts are supplied for an uneven hearth. If the fireplace is lower than the hearth, prop the unit up, thread the supplied bolts into the threaded inserts under the sides toward the rear, and set their depth to match the fireplace drop. Push the insert into position and adjust the bolts to level it.
Check clearances
Side of door to adjacent sidewall 15 in., to side facing 11 1/2 in. (facing max 3-1/2 in. deep); top of surround brow to mantel or top facing 16 in.; bottom of unit to ceiling 68 in.

Minimum clearances to combustibles when installed into a masonry fireplace:

Side of door → adjacent sidewall15 in. (380 mm)
Side of door → side facing (max 3-1/2 in. deep)11 1/2 in. (290 mm)
Top of surround brow → mantel16 in. (405 mm)
Top of surround brow → top facing16 in. (405 mm)
Bottom of unit → ceiling68 in. (1.7m)

Figure 14 shows the clearances as a drawing and also marks a mantel distance of 37 1/2" (955mm) measured from the hearth.
Prepare the fireplace

Have the chimney swept and inspected and repair cracks or loose mortar first. Lock the damper open or remove it; don't remove bricks or mortar, and fasten the supplied metal tag to the back wall if the fireplace was modified.

• Masonry wood-burning fireplace built to N.F.P.A. 211 or applicable code; chimney height 15' (minimum) from the hearth. Never connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.
  • Check for creosote buildup or obstructions, have the chimney swept and inspected, and complete repairs to cracks, loose mortar or other defects before installing.
  • Lock the existing damper open or remove it completely.
  • Don't remove bricks or mortar. Exception: masonry or steel, including the damper plate, may be removed from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame to fit a chimney liner, provided it doesn't weaken the fireplace and chimney or reduce protection for combustibles below the National Building Code.
  • If the fireplace was modified to fit the insert, fasten the supplied metal tag to its back wall.
  • The insert is heavy: install with two people, and cover the hearth with cardboard or a heavy blanket.
Note: the manual differs on factory-built fireplaces. The rating label (p. 3) says "install and use only in masonry or factory built fireplace"; p. 19 says "this Insert shall not be installed in a factory-built fireplace."
Liner, flue collar & set the insert

Feed the stainless liner down to a stove-to-liner adapter and fix the flue collar to it with three stainless screws and high temp stove cement. Remove trim, backing plate and baffle, push the insert in and level it, then pull the collar down and clamp it.

Full flue liner (required in Canada)

  1. Measure the chimney height from the top of the existing chimney flue to the floor of the hearth (this leaves extra liner for flashing and rain cap).
  2. Feed the stainless steel liner from the top of the chimney, through the damper area into the fireplace cavity. Attach a "stove to liner" adapter to the bottom per the liner manufacturer's instructions.
  3. Attach the flue collar (packed in the stove) to the adapter with three stainless screws. Caulk the connections with high temp stove cement; check the gasket is in good shape.
  4. Remove the front trim: lift each side, then pull it toward you to release the tabs.
  5. Remove the backing plate: two screws (T20 Torx) on each side, pull toward you, lift off.
  6. Remove the baffle (p. 13).
  7. Push the unit into the fireplace and level it with the rear adjustment legs.
  8. Reach through the flue opening and pull the collar down with the tool provided until its bolts pass through the mounting holes. Fit the clamps and nuts, centre the collar and tighten.
  9. Trim and shape a chimney-top flashing with a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side; seat it firmly on the flue tile over the liner.
  10. Attach a rain cap to the liner (a storm collar is optional).
  11. Re-install the backing plate, then the front trim, with the trim tabs fully engaged.

Direct flue connection (USA only, p. 21)

Measure from the top of the first chimney flue tile to the top of the insert, plus extra to insert into the tile. Feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile, attach the adapter, seal where the liner passes through the chimney throat, then follow steps 3–9 above. A clean-out door may be required by local code. Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner for correct draft.
Combustion air

Room air is drawn in through the front of the unit. For outside air, replace the fireplace ash clean-out cover with a rodent screen, keep the air inlet uncovered, and seal the surround to the fireplace.

Consult local building codes on combustion air. Two options:

  • Outside air: remove the cover from the ash clean-out in the existing fireplace and fit a rodent screen in its place. Install the insert without covering the air inlet opening, then seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter, so air is drawn from outside into the intake on the bottom of the appliance.
  • Room air: combustion air is drawn from the room through the front of the unit.
Power

Plug into a properly grounded outlet that accepts a three-pronged plug. Never route the cord under the unit or against hot or sharp surfaces; it can be moved to exit on the left, losing about 28.5" of usable length.

Don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Follow local codes, or CSA C22.2 (Canada) / ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA). The electrical rating is printed two ways; see the Electrical spec.

Moving the cord to the left side (p. 24)

  1. Lift and pull off the front trim. Remove the blower speed control knob with the supplied Allen key, then the backing plate, and disconnect the leads to the rocker switch.
  2. Remove the two screws (Torx T20) holding the electrical box and the wiring cover under the ash shelf.
  3. Move the strain relief from the right side of the wiring cover, re-route the cord through the left-side hole and re-install the strain relief with pliers.
  4. Remount the wire cover and electrical box, re-install the backing plate (reconnect the rocker switch leads), the knob and the front trim.

About 28.5"(725mm) of usable cord length is lost after switching sides.
Backing plate & front trim

Screw the backing plate to the casing-side mounting tabs (four screws), fit the blower speed control knob, connect the two power-supply wires to the rocker switch and screw it to the plate. Hook the front trim into its brackets and slide it down.

The front trim brackets are on either side of the firebox, between the blower bracket and the door. Line the hooks on the back of the trim up with the locking slots, push the trim in, then slide it down to engage the hooks.

Optional battery back-up (11490005, pp. 25–26)

  1. Open the battery box package.
  2. Lift up and pull to remove the front trim.
  3. Connect the battery box to the plug on the control board.
  4. Put the batteries in and place the box on the outside edge of the backing plate, wires facing down.
  5. Re-install the front trim.
Firebrick layout
If you install or replace the firebrick, start with the rear wall, then the side walls and floor, following the Figure 25 layout. A couple of small cut bricks are left over.

A9" x 4 1/2" x 1 1/4" (230 mm x 115 mm x 32 mm)
B2" x 9" x 1 1/4" (57 mm x 230 mm x 32 mm)
D2" x 4 7/16" x 1 1/4" (57mm x 113 mm x 32 mm)
E4 7/16" x 3 1/4" x 1 1/4 (113 mm x 83 mm x 32 mm)
Note: the firebrick table (p. 28) prints the 2" dimension of bricks B and D as 57 mm; the inch and metric figures don't match.
  1. Rear wall: stand two A bricks behind the right tab on the brick rail and slide them toward the centre; on the left, two A with one B between, slid toward the centre.
  2. Each side wall: E brick up into the back corner, then an A underneath; B up under the baffle tube box, then insert two A while holding the B in place. Repeat for the opposite wall.
  3. Floor: an A in each corner with one B, two A in front of the left rear A, then two A on the right and the D brick in the centre in front of the B.

Set: Firebrick, NEO 2.5 LE2, part 80002938 (p. 31). Burn only on the firebrick and replace broken or missing bricks.

fire.title: Lighting a fire
fire.html:
Never use chemicals, gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other volatile liquid to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep all such liquids well away from the insert while it is in use.

  1. Slide the air control (at the front, beneath the ash lip) to High, all the way to the left. Open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the insert. Crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it, then add a few pieces of large kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" (13mm) to 1" (25mm) until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame. Never leave the insert unattended with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small pieces of wood and close the door.
  5. Begin normal burning once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred.
Your first 2–3 fires bake on the paint. Ventilate the room well (open all windows and doors), as the fumes can bother some people. Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures. Don't disconnect them.
Build the fire directly on the firebricks, never on a grate or andirons. Keep the door closed whenever it's burning, and open it only to add wood.

air.title: Air control & reloading
air.html:
The air control sits at the front, beneath the ash lip. Facing the insert, slide it right for Low and left for High; the middle is about Medium. Any position in between works for the heat you want.

High: lighting and reloading

After adding wood, burn on High for about 10 to 15 minutes, or until the wood is fully charred. Don't run on High for long periods: you risk over-firing.

Low: overnight burns

Unsplit logs are best. Char the wood completely on High first, then slowly turn the air down to Low.

To reload

  1. Move the air to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't come out.
  3. Load logs up to 18" (457mm) long, parallel to the front, with space for air between them. Don't load so high that opening the door would be hazardous.

Restarting from overnight coals: rake the hot embers to the front, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to High. Once the wood has charred, reset the air.

Over-firing: a glowing red top or vent pipe means it's over-firing. That can permanently damage the insert and chimney, is hazardous if not corrected, and may void the warranty.

wood.title: Burning the right wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood gives higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwood or green, freshly cut hardwood. Season wood for six months or more and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat sources.

Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Note: the manual differs on wet wood. Its do-not-burn list (p. 6) includes wet or green wood and unseasoned wood, and p. 5 says not to burn wet wood; p. 8 says that if you feel you must burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air control set open enough to keep a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and never try to burn green or wet wood overnight.

Test a piece

Add a large piece to a good, large bed of coals:

  • Dry: it burns on more than one side within one minute.
  • Damp: it turns black and lights within three minutes.
  • Soaked: it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Wet or green wood, unseasoned wood, treated or salt-water wood, garbage, coal or charcoal, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, construction or demolition debris, solvents, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products, paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard, manure or animal remains, or anything containing rubber (including tires), plastic or asbestos. Salt-water wood and garbage destroy metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the insert.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

blower.title: Blowers & power
blower.html:
Your insert has twin variable-speed blowers that circulate warm air. A rocker switch picks the mode and a speed knob sets the speed.

Rocker at "O": automaticBlowers start once the insert reaches operating temperature, and stop after the fire is out and it has cooled
Rocker at "--": manualBypasses the temperature switch for full control

Suggested speeds

  • Air control on Low ("L", pushed to the far right): run the blower on Low.
  • Air control anywhere above Low: any blower speed you like.

If the power goes out

The insert still operates within safe and certified limits using the manual air control at the front. With the optional battery back-up (part 11490005), it stays fully functional during a power failure.

Vacuum the blowers at least every six months to clear dust and debris. Reaching them means removing the front trim and backing plate, so unplug the insert first.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
If the glass darkens from slow burning or poor wood, clean it with fireplace glass cleaner once the insert is cold.

  • Never clean the glass while it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that might scratch.
  • Don't slam the door or knock the glass. Check that no logs stick out to hit the glass as you close the door.

What the film tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion, dry wood, and fairly clean pipes and chimney. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. That deposit is building up at least as fast in your chimney.

Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the insert again. Use only 18" (457mm) x 10-1/4" (260mm) x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer, no other type.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the insert is cold. Once the ash is 3" (76mm) to 4" (102mm) deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the excess. Leave about 1" (25 mm) of ash on the firebox bottom: it helps keep a hot charcoal bed.

Storing ashes safely

  • Put them in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  • Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything combustible, until final disposal.
  • If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all the cinders have thoroughly cooled.
  • Don't put other waste in that container.
Keep the front of the firebox, where boost combustion air comes in, clear of heavy ash buildup so it doesn't block the air flow.

chimney.title: Chimney & creosote
chimney.html:
Burning wood slowly makes tar and vapours that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot. Some creosote is inevitable; regular inspection and cleaning is the answer.

  • Have the chimney connector and chimney inspected at least once every two months in the heating season.
  • If creosote has built up to 3 mm or more, have it removed.
  • Until you know your insert, check for creosote daily. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.

Burn cleaner

Use dry, seasoned wood and plenty of air. Small loads (two or three logs, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load) burn cleanest. After each reload, leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes; after about 30 minutes you can turn it down a lot.

Before the chimney is swept, move the flue thermocouple out of the way: remove the top grill (two screws), pull the Flue Thermocouple Guide out as far as it goes, and push it back in after cleaning.

safety.title: Chimney fire & safety
safety.html:
Signs of a chimney fire

  • Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney
  • A roaring sound
  • Vibration of the chimney

If it happens

  1. Get ready to evacuate. Have a plan everyone understands and a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the insert.
  3. Call the local fire department. Have a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Once it's out, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks before you light another fire. Check combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.

Every day

  • The insert is hot while burning. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Hot glass will cause burns; never let children touch it.
  • Burn wood cleanly: don't burn wet wood, and don't turn the insert down too quickly after loading.
  • Avoid excessively hot fires: household trash, cardboard, Christmas tree limbs, or a full load on hot coals with the air wide open longer than it takes to char it.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended where the insert is installed.

maint.title: Maintenance checks
maint.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping:

Weekly

  • Firebrick: look for cracking. Replace broken or missing bricks.
  • Door gasket: sagging, placement, damage.

Monthly

  • Brick rails and brick rail tabs
  • Air riser tube at the back of the firebox
  • Back side of the airwash chamber
  • Baffle locking pin and baffle tubes

When the chimney is cleaned

Top baffle board / blanket, baffle, top heat shield and its mounting bolts, baffle gasket, brick rails and manifold.

Some baffle warping (up to 1/4" or .65cm) is normal. Replace the baffle if it's permanently warped more than that, cracked or broken. Never run the insert with the baffle, tubes or insulation removed.

Door gasket: 3/4" (19mm) fiberglass rope that needs only light pressure to seal. The replacement kit is part# 80000670 from your Pacific Energy dealer. Call your dealer about any damage: running with broken parts can damage other parts and may void the warranty.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 years comprehensive, parts and laborAny defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage.
  • Firebox rails and heat shields (not in the lifetime warranty).
  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets.
  • Any part showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance, or modification.

Premature wear points to improper use, such as excessive draft, heating too large an area or contaminated fuel, and may void the warranty. Tampering with the air control, or burning salt-water wood or garbage, voids it.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. Register online at pacificenergy.net/register; the serial number is on the certification label or the manual cover.

specOutput.title: Output, efficiency & emissions
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output (table)13,240 to 29,536 btu/hr
Rating statement13,200 to 29,500 Btu/hr
Maker's website: EPA Test Fuel Output 29,500 BTU.
Maker's website: Peak Output (Cordwood) 85,000 BTU.
HHV tested efficiency73%
LHV tested efficiency79%
EPA certified emissions1.6 grams per hour
CO emissions1.6 grams per minute

Meets the U.S. EPA 2020 cribwood particulate emission standards, tested to EPA Method 28R. Efficiencies are weighted averages from CSA B415 testing; the output range uses the low and high EPA test burn rates with Douglas Fir dimensional lumber.

Both output ranges are on p. 3. The rating statement gives the range rounded to the nearest hundred, 13,200 to 29,500 Btu/hr; the efficiency table gives 13,240 to 29,536 btu/hr.

The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered (p. 7).

specFuel.title: Fuel & wood length
specFuel.html:
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Maximum wood length18 inches
Ideal wood length17 inches

Solid fuel (cordwood) only. Load wood parallel to the stove front, up to 18"(457mm), with air space between logs. No grate or andirons: build the fire directly on the firebrick. Operate only with the feed door closed; replace glass only with ceramic glass.

specFireplace.title: Fireplace requirements
specFireplace.html:
FireplaceMasonry, wood-burning (N.F.P.A. 211 or local code)
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)
DamperLocked open or removed

The fireplace and chimney must be suitable for wood burning: check for creosote or obstructions, have the chimney swept and inspected, and complete repairs (cracks, loose mortar) before installing. The installation shall conform to CAN/CSA-B365, Installation Code for Solid-Fuel-Burning Appliances and Equipment. Minimum fireplace opening dimensions are shown only as a drawing (Figure 12, p. 16).

Note: the manual differs on factory-built fireplaces. The rating label (p. 3) says "install and use only in masonry or factory built fireplace"; p. 19 says "this Insert shall not be installed in a factory-built fireplace."

specFlue.title: Flue & liner
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D., removable
CanadaContinuous liner, class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640 (required)
USAFlue liner to UL-1777, or direct flue connection
Recommended draft.06"w.c. - .09" w.c. when hot, on high

In Canada the liner runs from the insert's flue collar to the top of the chimney. Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner everywhere: it drafts correctly and prevents difficult start-ups and smoking out the door. Direct flue connection is permitted only in the USA (p. 21); it needs a seal in the chimney throat, and local code may require a clean-out door.

Too much draft causes excessive temperatures (an uncontrollable burn, glowing red parts); too little causes back puffing, chimney plugging and smoke leaking at joints (p. 10).

conflicts.issue: The DO NOT BURN list (p. 6) includes "Wet or green wood" and "Unseasoned wood", and To Avoid a Chimney Fire (p. 5) says "Do not burn wet wood or turn down the unit too quickly after loading"; p. 8 says "If you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures. Do not attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood." Both shown in an amber note; p. 5's rule is also in the safety drawer.

review.notes: Wood insert: no ignition system; lighting is the newspaper-and-kindling procedure on p. 7. Figure-only content not transcribed: overall insert dimensions (Fig. 7, p. 14), minimum fireplace opening (Fig. 12, p. 16), the ember-protection drawing (Fig. 13, p. 17, whose labels look inconsistent, e.g. 'CAN 18” / 405mm', 'CAN: 20 1/4” / 610mm', 'USA: 18 1/4”'), the wiring diagram (Fig. 17, p. 23), firebrick layout (Fig. 25) and parts diagram (p. 32). Surround sizes are printed as lettered dimensions A/B (p. 14); the text doesn't say which is width or height. The 37 1/2" (955mm) mantel distance from the hearth is a Figure 14 label. The p. 18 text says clearances are shown 'in Figure 13', but the clearance drawing is Figure 14. CO emissions are printed as '1.6 grams per minute' (p. 3), the same figure as the 1.6 g/hr particulate rating; transcribed as printed. Blower rocker switch positions are transcribed as extracted ('O' automatic, '--' manual). The optional battery box (11490005) battery type and count are not stated. The lifetime warranty is printed as 'LTD Lifetime Coverage (10 years)'. The manual does not give heating area, maximum cordwood BTU, burn time, firebox volume or blower cfm, so those catalog specs could not be checked; catalog efficiency (73% HHV), emissions (1.6 g/hr), log lengths (18/17 in.), flue (6 in.) and EPA output (29,500, matching the rating statement) agree. The catalog's regular 'trim (36 x 26 in.)' may be a different part from the manual's 'regular surround'; flagged so a reviewer can check. Bilingual text is limited to the rating label; nothing was French-only. Pages 34-35 are blank.
